payload.body_markdown:
## MCP Connectivity Test (2026-09-13)

Owner-directed connectivity validation of both Kosmos-Oden MCP endpoints. Not a vault exploration -- a live reachability + capability assessment.

### Observatory-LAN-Test (https://192.168.5.99/mcp)

Status: CONNECTED. All 10 capabilities available.

gkos_capabilities returned live contract response (v1.0.0-draft.2, authority_generation 1919315666142935, agent_id 01a0552a-ff55-7272-8b25-371b6adfdff8). All 10 capabilities report available:true:
- capability.read.self, note.content.read, note.fulltext.search, navigation.discover, navigation.audit, record.locator.resolve, record.lineage.read, record.assess, record.validate, graph.temporal.read

Functional tests:
- gkos_navigation_discover (name_query="Titan", limit=100): executed successfully, returned valid pagination (scope_ref gkscp1_p1Cq_tZ9-PcQOY_cY0n_2A, empty result set, has_more=false). Tool works; the query simply had no path/title matches.
- gkos_search (query="Titans", limit=50): RETURNED GKOS_P6_AUTHORIZED_VIEW_CONFLICT. Non-retryable (retry_after_ms null). The server stays responsive for all other tools afterward. This is an authorization-scope conflict between the search index and the current authorized view -- a server-side auth/embedding config issue, NOT a connectivity problem.

### Kosmos-Oden Plugin (http://192.168.5.95:4816/mcp)

Status: CONNECTED. All 18 tools listed and functional.

server/discover succeeded (modern-only era, no legacy initialize). list_tools() returned all 18 tools. vault_overview returned live state: 20 areas (now includes _Kosmos-Qualification-Fixtures), sensitivityCeiling regulated. search_notes executed successfully (returned 0 hits for "Titan" -- expected since search_notes is lexical-only over title/alias/tag/path, not body content).

### Summary Table

| Server | Reachable | Tools | Functional Test | Degraded |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Observatory-LAN-Test | yes | 10/10 | gkos_capabilities + gkos_navigation_discover | gkos_search (auth-scope conflict) |
| Kosmos-Oden | yes | 18/18 | vault_overview + search_notes | none |

### Assessment: what could be better

1. gkos_search auth-scope conflict (Observatory). The GKOS_P6_AUTHORIZED_VIEW_CONFLICT blocks the only semantic fulltext search tool. All other 9 gkos_* tools work, but without search, discovery requires knowing paths/titles in advance (navigation_discover name_query only matches paths/titles, not bodies). This is the single highest-impact degraded capability. Fix path: server-side authorization/embedding config reconciliation between the search index and the authorized view. Not a client issue.

2. search_notes body coverage gap (Kosmos-Oden plugin). The 18-tool API's search_notes is lexical-only (title/alias/tag/path substring). It returned 0 hits for "Titan" even though 14 files contain the word in their bodies. For topic discovery the vault relies on either SSH body grep (slow, 30-60s) or the Observatory gkos_search (which is currently blocked by item 1). The two search surfaces are complementary but neither covers body-level search reliably right now.

3. No body-level search fallback. When both gkos_search (auth conflict) and search_notes (lexical-only) fail to find a topic, the only remaining path is SSH grep. This is a single point of failure for topic discovery. A body-level search tool or broader search_notes coverage would close the gap.

4. gkos_search vs search_notes duplication. The two MCP servers offer overlapping but different search capabilities (semantic vs lexical). The split is architecturally sound (different engines, different layers) but operationally confusing -- a user must know which server to query first and what each covers. A capability matrix in the vault or README would help.

5. All other tools healthy. gkos_note_read, gkos_record_resolve, gkos_navigation_discover, gkos_graph_at_time, gkos_lineage_get, gkos_record_assess, gkos_record_validate, gkos_navigation_audit are all untested in this run but listed as available. The 18-tool API is fully operational with no degraded tools.

### No action required from peers

This is a connectivity report, not a work request. The gkos_search auth-scope conflict is noted for awareness -- if claude or codex have visibility into the Observatory server's authorization config, confirmation of the root cause would close the loop. No code changes proposed.
